Love letters · say it loud

Say it the way you mean it.

One wide, open page — write what you wish to say, in your own words, with a few nudges beside it if you get stuck. Pick a tone and a paper, and keep it as a file.

One open blank, your own words — the letter carries exactly what you write here.

Need a nudge? Steal a starting line — or think about one of these:

  • A moment with them you keep replaying
  • One small thing they do that you quietly love
  • Something you have never said out loud
  • What you hope for the two of you

The letter below is editable — click into it and rewrite any line. What you see is exactly what downloads.

From scratch · your rules

A blank page. Fill it your way.

No template at all — just your name for them, your photos, stickers and up to six little pages. Preview it as a gift, then download it and send it.

How a blank gift opens

1 · A cover with your title and their name.
2 · Each page opens with a tap, in the order you wrote them.
3 · A final page with your closing line and a burst of confetti.

A little extra: type ♥ or ★ into a page as a sticker, or simply write your own words.

Tip: keep each page to one thought. Short pages feel like unwrapping; long ones feel like homework.

How it works · easy, promise

From a feeling → to something they can open.

1

Pick the moment

Tap Make a gift above, then choose the moment — birthday, missing someone, saying thank you — or start from a blank page. Each choice opens its own page, with only that maker on it.

2

Make it theirs

Add names, a photo, your message and one memory. Watch the preview change as you type. Change anything until it sounds like you.

3

Send the magic

You get a temporary gift link for WhatsApp — the gift itself, packed small, ending with a 10-letter gift ID made just for that gift, that opens the gift for 30 days — plus a gift code as a fallback, a readable PDF, or the full playable file. They open it in a browser — no app or account needed.

Before you ask · real talk

A few things you might be wondering…

Can I make a gift for anyone?

Yes. Pick a template, answer its questions in your own words, and share the link. Every template, mini gift, date invite and letter works end to end, just as you see it here.

Does the person I send it to need an app or an account?

No. The downloaded gift is a single file that opens in any phone or computer browser. No app to install, no account to create, no sign-in.

How do I actually send a gift?

Personalise a template and press “Share gift”. You get a temporary gift link to send on WhatsApp — the gift itself, packed small, ending with a 10-letter gift ID made just for that gift, that opens the interactive gift when tapped and stops opening after 30 days — plus a gift code as a fallback, a PDF download (readable, for WhatsApp or anywhere), or the full playable gift file — send that file on WhatsApp, email or any messenger, just like sending a photo. Keep a copy for yourself too.

Can I change a gift after I have made it?

Yes — come back here, make it again with your changes, and download a fresh file. Nothing is stored online, so edits are simply a new version of the file.

What happens to my photos and words?

They stay in your browser tab while you work. They are never uploaded, never stored, and they disappear when you close the tab. The only copy that exists is the file you choose to download.

Can I use this on my phone?

Yes. The whole page — browsing, personalising, previews and downloads — is built to work on phone screens as well as on a computer.

Tap to open this gift link ↗

This is a temporary gift link. The gift travels inside it, packed as small as it can be without a server, and it ends with the gift’s 10-letter ID — a different ID is made for every gift. Tapping it opens the gift on DilSeCanvas, with its taps, candles and envelopes — no pasting needed. It stops opening after 30 days.

If the link doesn’t come through, send this code instead. The person who gets it pastes it in the “Received a gift?” box at the top of this page. Photos can’t travel inside a link or a code, so those versions use text only.
